hits.name: James Clear
hits.media_note: text-only; replies limited to mentioned users (not a reply target)
hits.text: You can be authentic and hardworking and still struggle to find your footing if you're in the wrong environment.
hits.full_text:
You can be authentic and hardworking and still struggle to find your footing if you're in the wrong environment.

-A fun person trapped in the wrong city.
-A loving partner in a relationship that won't reciprocate.
-A great entrepreneur stuck in the wrong business.

Think about your placement as much as your performance. Plant yourself where you can thrive.
hits.hook: JamesClear: think about your placement as much as your performance
hits.draft_en:
If something isn't working, it might not need more effort. It might need a different chair.

A different hour, a different table, nothing on it but paper. Try the small move before the big push.

reply_ideas.reply_text: The magazine-article trick is such a good reframe. 'Write a book' is too big to sit down to, but one piece that can stand on its own is something you can actually start. Also weirdly comforting that the first four chapters went in the trash.
The kind of urgency that helps me is small and specific. Not 'change everything,' just 'do the piece I keep putting off, today.' The big version tips into panic way too fast.
The idea museum is the part I'd underline. An idea you don't write down is gone by lunch, and a body of work is mostly those small captures piling up over years. Paper works fine for it, too.
